changes.after: A struct groups named pieces of data. Each piece is called a field.

before: A struct groups named fields. A field of type String owns its string data; assigning that field to another binding moves it unless it is explicitly borrowed or cloned.

After moving one non-Copy field, that field cannot be used through the original value. Other independent Copy fields can still be used when the type has no custom Drop implementation. Do not describe every struct assignment as a deep copy.
Expected output or behavior: Rust 15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Borrow &session.topic instead and explain why the owner remains usable. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A struct groups named pieces of data. Each piece is called a field.
Assigning the String field to `topic` moves that text. The minutes field is still available.
The output is `Rust 15`. The print uses the new owner of the text and the unchanged minutes field.

before.question: If the print tries session.topic instead of topic after the move, what happens?
choices: It prints Rust twice because every field is copied.
The moved field becomes an empty string.
Compilation rejects use of the moved String field.
before.explanation: Moving session.topic transfers ownership; the original field is no longer available to read.

after.question: Can the print read `session.topic` after the move?
choices: Yes. The whole struct was copied.
Yes. Moving a field clears only its first letter.
No. That String moved to another name.
after.explanation: The String field now belongs to topic. Using its old place is not allowed.
